surfaces: Terminal CLI (npm global install -> `gemini` / `gemini.cmd` shim, runs under node.exe). Also embedded as an ACP agent server (packages/cli/src/acp/acpSession.ts) and bundled with the VS Code IDE companion extension, but both reuse the same core ChatRecordingService and therefore the same on-disk format. Not a VS Code/JetBrains extension with a globalStorage state.vscdb — no SQLite involved, no new Rust dependency needed.
binaries: npm bin `gemini` (POSIX) / `gemini.cmd` (Windows shim -> node.exe). No native .exe is shipped. Process basename on Windows is therefore `node.exe` or `cmd.exe`, NOT `gemini`, so the existing Provider::from_executable("gemini") -> Provider::Gemini (web Gemini) mapping cannot be reused for the CLI without a collision.

paths: %USERPROFILE%\.gemini\tmp\<project-slug>\chats\<parentSessionId>\<subagentSessionId>.jsonl   (subagent session, nested under the parent session id)
%USERPROFILE%\.gemini\tmp\<project-slug>\.project_root   (ownership marker file; contains the absolute project root path, lowercased on Windows)
%USERPROFILE%\.gemini\tmp\<project-slug>\logs.json   (legacy debug log, whole-file rewrite, JSON array - not a session log)
%USERPROFILE%\.gemini\tmp\<project-slug>\logs\session-<sessionId>.jsonl   (ActivityLogger console/network capture, opt-in only - NOT a session log)
storage.format: JSONL — one JSON object per line, newline-delimited, UTF-8. No SQLite, no protobuf, no encryption, no auth token required to read. Line 1 is a session-metadata record; subsequent lines are message records, {$set:...} metadata patches, {$patch:...} message patches, or {$rewindTo:"..."}. Legacy single-JSON-document `.json` session files still exist on disk from older versions and are migrated to `.jsonl` on resume (chatRecordingService.ts:732-733, 970-973).
storage.append_semantics: APPEND-ONLY and live. ChatRecordingService.appendRecord() does `fs.appendFileSync(this.conversationFile, JSON.stringify(record) + '\n')` (chatRecordingService.ts:942-958, shipped 0.65.0 build line 779). Every user turn, model turn, tool-call batch and metadata update is flushed to disk immediately, so a notify file-watcher sees new bytes mid-run. The one exception is rewriteConversationFile() (atomic temp+rename), used only to recover an unreadable resumed session.
storage.session_file_naming: Main: `session-` + `new Date().toISOString().slice(0,16)` with ':' -> '-' + '-' + first 8 chars of the sanitized session UUID, e.g. `session-2026-06-13T05-26-b2e9ca8f.jsonl` (SESSION_FILE_PREFIX='session-' in chatRecordingTypes.ts:12). On filename collision an index is inserted: `session-<ts>-1-<shortId>.jsonl`. Subagent: `<sanitizedSessionId>.jsonl` inside `chats/<sanitizedParentSessionId>/`. Legacy pre-JSONL files were `chats/session-<ts>.json` (single JSON document).

fields.model: YES. `model` on every type:'gemini' message record (e.g. "gemini-2.5-pro"), set by GeminiChat.recordCompletedToolCalls()/recordMessage().
fields.tool_name: YES. `toolCalls[].name` — canonical names verified in packages/core/src/tools/definitions/base-declarations.ts: read_file, write_file, replace, run_shell_command, read_many_files, list_directory, glob, grep_search, google_web_search, web_fetch, write_todos, get_internal_docs, activate_skill, ask_user, enter_plan_mode, exit_plan_mode, update_topic, complete_task, invoke_agent, tracker_*_task, read_mcp_resource, list_mcp_resources, mcp__*/discovered_tool_*.
fields.tool_arguments: YES. `toolCalls[].args` is a JSON object. File-bearing keys: `file_path` (read_file, write_file, replace — confirmed in the shipped 0.65.0 write-file.js:41 / edit.js:267), `include` (array of globs, read_many_files), `path` (list_directory), `pattern` (glob, grep_search), `command` (run_shell_command). NOTE: `write_file.args.content` holds the entire file body and `replace.args.old_string`/`new_string` hold source code — these must never be forwarded.
fields.tool_result: YES. `toolCalls[].result` (PartListUnion) plus `status` ('validating'|'scheduled'|'executing'|'awaiting_approval'|'success'|'error'|'cancelled'). Also `toolCalls[].displayName`, `.description`, `.resultDisplay`, `.agentId`, `.timestamp`. Tool results are also delivered later as a `{$patch:{toolCalls:[{id,result}]}}` record. Must never be forwarded.
fields.current_file_path: YES for the file currently being touched: `toolCalls[].args.file_path` (relative or absolute). `read_many_files.args.include[]` and `list_directory.args.path` are directory/glob level.
fields.workspace_project_path: NOT in the session file for main sessions. The metadata record carries `projectHash` = sha256(projectRoot) (paths.ts getProjectHash), which is one-way. Recoverable from the sibling marker file `<root>/<slug>/.project_root` (absolute project root, lowercased on Windows) or from `%USERPROFILE%\.gemini\projects.json` (keys are lowercased absolute paths on Windows). Subagent metadata records DO carry `directories` (absolute workspace dirs) — chatRecordingService.ts:825-832, 1248-1255.
fields.turn_phase_boundaries: PARTIAL. A type:'user' record = turn start (TaskStarted). A type:'gemini' record with text and no toolCalls = final answer (TerminalCandidate). There is NO explicit turn-end / session-complete record, so ParsedEvent::Completed can never fire; the session instead goes inactive through Discodex's existing TERMINAL_DEBOUNCE_MS=4000 after a TerminalCandidate.
fields.timestamps: YES. ISO-8601 / RFC3339 with milliseconds and 'Z' (new Date().toISOString()) on every message record and on every tool call record; `startTime`/`lastUpdated` on the metadata record. Discodex's existing events::timestamp_ms() already parses RFC3339, and events::line_timestamp_ms() already looks at the top-level `timestamp` key — so no timestamp helper changes are required.
fields.thoughts: type:'gemini' records carry `thoughts[]` (ThoughtSummary with subject/description). Present but must be reduced to `Thinking { reasoning: None }` — thought text is conversation content.
fields.ordering: Ordered. Append order == event order. The same message `id` can appear on multiple lines (the model turn is written once, then rewritten with the toolCalls array after the tools complete) — last occurrence wins, so a tailer must tolerate duplicate ids.

parser_strategy:
New provider variant `Provider::GeminiCli` (the existing `Provider::Gemini` is the web chat app and must not be reused). New `parse_gemini_cli_line(line)` in events.rs, dispatched from `parse_line_for`.

Record discrimination (all from one JSONL line):
1. Metadata record: has string `sessionId` AND string `projectHash` -> session identity. `kind` == 'subagent' -> emit `SubagentSpawned { conversation_id: <subagent sessionId>, agent: "Gemini Subagent" }`; for subagents, `directories[0]` is an absolute workspace dir -> emit `SessionMetadata { project, cwd }`. For kind == 'main' there is no cwd in the file, so the project is resolved from the path (see discodex_plan). `summary` / `memoryScratchpad` / `lastUpdated` are ignored (summary is conversation content).
2. Message record: has `id` + `type`.
   - type == 'user'  -> `TaskStarted { started_at_ms: timestamp }` (RFC3339, parsed by the existing events::timestamp_ms). The `content` parts are dropped entirely.
   - type == 'gemini':
       * if `model` is a string -> `AgentDetected { agent: model }` (e.g. "gemini-2.5-pro").
       * if `toolCalls` is a non-empty array -> for each entry: `TrackedToolStarted { call_id: tc.id, activity }` immediately followed by `TrackedToolFinished { call_id: tc.id }`. Gemini only persists a tool call once it has COMPLETED (GeminiChat.recordCompletedToolCalls, geminiChat.ts:1807-1841, called from useGeminiStream.ts:364-390 after the scheduler resolves the batch), so start+finish are emitted together; `finish_tool` leaves `current_file` intact in state.rs, so the file stays visible.
       * else if the record carries text `content` and no toolCalls -> `TerminalCandidate` (the model produced its final answer for the turn).
       * else -> `Thinking { reasoning: None }` (covers thought-only turns; `thoughts[]` text is never read).
   - type == 'info' | 'error' | 'warning' -> ignored.
3. `{$set: {...}}` -> ignored (would leak `summary`).
4. `{$patch: {id, toolCalls:[{id,result}]}}` -> for each patched tool call id emit `TrackedToolFinished { call_id }`; the `result` payload is never read.
5. `{$rewindTo: "..."}` -> ignored.

ToolActivity construction (whitelist only):
- name -> label via a Gemini-specific mapper (the shared classify_tool() maps "replace" to "Using development tools", so it needs a Gemini table): read_file/read_many_files/list_directory -> "Reading project files"; write_file/replace -> "Editing files"; run_shell_command -> classify_tool(name, args.command) so cargo/npm/git special-cases still work; glob/grep_search -> "Searching project"; google_web_search/web_fetch -> "Browsing documentation"; write_todos/enter_plan_mode/exit_plan_mode -> "Planning changes"; ask_user -> "Waiting for input"; activate_skill/invoke_agent -> "Running coding agent"; default -> "Using development tools".
- file -> extract_file_basename(args) already handles "file_path" and "path" (events.rs:659-691); "include" (read_many_files) is an array and is deliberately not read.
- language -> language_from_file(basename).
- NEVER read: args.content, args.old_string, args.new_string, args.command (raw), result, content, thoughts, description, displayName, resultDisplay.

No watcher.rs or main.rs format machinery is required beyond the project-root lookup, because the format is append-only newline-delimited JSON — the existing LogTailer works verbatim.

risks: Executable-name collision: `gemini` is already mapped to Provider::Gemini (the web app) in Provider::from_executable, and the CLI ships no .exe (it runs under node.exe / gemini.cmd), so focused-window detection for the CLI is unreliable. Since the CLI gets real session tracking, keep the existing web mapping and add only `gemini-cli`/`geminicli`/`gemini.cmd` -> GeminiCli plus a careful from_window rule (a title that is exactly 'gemini' or ends with ' - gemini' but NOT gemini.google.com, which is matched earlier).

Project name case: ProjectRegistry.normalizePath lowercases the path on win32, so `.project_root` and `projects.json` yield a LOWERCASED workspace folder name ('discodex' instead of 'Discodex'). The slug fallback is also lowercased. Only the directory slug is available with original case, and it is lossy for names containing spaces/dots ('My App' -> 'my-app').

Tool activity is recorded only at COMPLETION, not at dispatch, so the Discord presence shows the previous tool's file while a long tool is running. Codex logs the call at start, so Gemini will feel slightly less live.

Format churn: the session format moved from a single-JSON `.json` document to append-only `.jsonl` inside the 0.4x line, and the project directory moved from a sha256 hash to a human slug (ProjectRegistry migration). The recommended is_session_log rule is directory-shape based (must live under a 'chats' directory) rather than filename based, so it survives both migrations. Legacy `.json` files should be rejected by is_session_log because the existing tailer is line-delimited and would mis-parse them; if legacy support is wanted later it needs a separate whole-file read path in watcher.rs.

is_session_log must be path-aware, not just filename based: `<tmp>/<slug>/logs/session-<id>.jsonl` (ActivityLogger) and `<tmp>/<slug>/logs.json` also match a naive `session-*.jsonl` rule. The rule must require the file to live under a directory literally named 'chats' (parent or grandparent).

Privacy blast radius: one JSONL line contains the user's prompt, the assistant's text, thought summaries, full file bodies (write_file.args.content), old/new source strings (replace), the raw shell command, and the full tool output. The parser must whitelist fields and never serialise a whole record into an error message or log line.
No explicit turn-end or session-complete record exists, so ParsedEvent::Completed is unreachable; rely on TerminalCandidate + the existing 4s terminal debounce to make the session go inactive.

rewriteConversationFile() replaces a session file atomically (temp + rename) when a resumed file is unreadable. If the replacement is shorter than the tailer's cursor the existing LogTailer resets to offset 0 and re-reads the file, replaying the conversation and re-firing TaskStarted (resetting the elapsed timer). Rare, but it should be watched for; a length-guard on the Gemini provider would be the mitigation.

Session pruning is upstream's job (default general.sessionRetention maxAge 30d, maxCount 50), and recent_logs() only keeps the newest 8 files, so a burst of parallel sessions in one project could push the active one out of the watch set.
confidence: High for the storage layout, format, append semantics, record grammar, tool names/arg keys and model id — all verified directly against upstream main AND against the published @google/gemini-cli / @google/gemini-cli-core 0.65.0 npm artifacts, plus a real user's on-disk paths in upstream issue #27877. Medium only for the exact timing of the tool-call record (COMPLETION-only, inferred from the call chain useGeminiStream -> GeminiChat.recordCompletedToolCalls -> ChatRecordingService.recordToolCalls, all read in source) and for the Windows lowercasing of the project name (ProjectRegistry.normalizePath). Not verified: any hypothetical post-0.65.0 format change (UNVERIFIED), and the actual casing of the published project folder name on a real Windows install (the source says lowercased; I did not inspect any local ~/.gemini per instructions).
discodex_plan:
PROVIDER VARIANT
- `Provider::GeminiCli` (new; keep `Provider::Gemini` for the web app). display_name() -> "Gemini CLI".
- logo_url() -> "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@lobehub/icons-static-png@1.97.0/dark/geminicli-color.png" (verified 200 image/png; this is the Gemini CLI product asset, not the Gemini chat/parent icon already used by Provider::Gemini).
- has_session_tracking() -> true; default_activity() -> "Working with coding agent".
- from_executable: add "gemini-cli" | "geminicli" | "gemini.cmd" -> GeminiCli. DO NOT steal "gemini" (already the web provider).
- from_window: add a terminal rule for a title that is exactly "gemini" or ends with " - gemini" / " — gemini" (Windows Terminal tab), placed AFTER the existing "gemini.google.com" rule so the web app is unaffected. The CLI ships no .exe, so exe-name detection will usually miss it; session tracking is the primary path.

SESSION SOURCE ROOT
  SessionSource { provider: Provider::GeminiCli, root: home.join(".gemini").join("tmp") }
  -> %USERPROFILE%\.gemini\tmp
  (upstream: Storage.getGlobalTempDir() = <runtimeDir>/tmp, runtimeDir = <home>/.gemini; docs/reference/commands.md L87 documents C:\Users\<YourUsername>\.gemini\tmp\<project_hash>\)
  Note: GEMINI_CLI_HOME can relocate the whole ~/.gemini tree; also macOS sandbox-exec reroutes to ~/.cache/gemini. Neither applies to Windows, but the root expression should be the default.

is_session_log RULE (provider.rs) — must be path-aware, not filename-only:
  if provider == Provider::GeminiCli {
      if !lower_filename.ends_with(".jsonl") { return false; }              // excludes legacy single-JSON .json files
      let parent_is_chats  = path.parent().file_name()  == "chats";        // <tmp>/<slug>/chats/<file>.jsonl
      let grand_is_chats   = path.parent().parent().file_name() == "chats"; // <tmp>/<slug>/chats/<parentId>/<file>.jsonl
      return parent_is_chats || grand_is_chats;
  }
  This deliberately rejects <tmp>/<slug>/logs/session-<id>.jsonl (the opt-in ActivityLogger console/network capture), <tmp>/<slug>/logs.json, checkpoints/, shell_history, plans/, memory/, tool-outputs/.

PROJECT / CWD RESOLUTION (the one piece of extra machinery)
  The main-session metadata record contains no cwd (only a one-way sha256 projectHash). Two supported sources, both verified upstream:
    (a) <root>/<slug>/.project_root  -> absolute project root (lowercased on win32). Written by ProjectRegistry.ensureOwnershipMarkers for baseDir = getGlobalTempDir().
    (b) %USERPROFILE%\.gemini\projects.json -> { "<lowercased abs project path>": "<slug>" }.
  Recommendation: add `events::parse_line_for_path(provider, path, line)` (a thin wrapper) that, for GeminiCli, resolves the project once per file and prepends `SessionMetadata { project, cwd }` when the parsed line is the metadata record. Change the two call sites in main.rs (apply_lines_at L537, apply_historical_lines L552) from parse_line_for(provider,&line) to parse_line_for_path(provider,path,&line). Cache the resolved (project,cwd) per path in the worker to avoid re-reading .project_root on every notify event.
  Resolution algorithm: from <root>/<slug>/chats/... take the component two levels above 'chats' as the slug; read <root>/<slug>/.project_root (trim, tolerate CRLF); cwd = that string, project = project_name(cwd) (existing helper, events.rs:1087). Fallback if the marker is missing: cwd = slug, project = slug.
  For subagent metadata records, `directories[0]` is already an absolute workspace dir and can be used directly as cwd.
  Privacy note: only the FINAL FOLDER NAME is emitted; the full path stays inside the parser and is never published.

PARSE MAPPING (events.rs) — see parser_strategy above for the full table. Summary:
  metadata record (sessionId+projectHash)  -> SessionMetadata (path-resolved) / SubagentSpawned for kind=='subagent'
  type=='user'                             -> TaskStarted { started_at_ms: <RFC3339 timestamp> }
  type=='gemini' + model                  -> AgentDetected { agent: <model id> }
  type=='gemini' + toolCalls[]             -> TrackedToolStarted{ id, activity } + TrackedToolFinished{ id } per call
  type=='gemini' + text, no toolCalls      -> TerminalCandidate
  type=='gemini' + thoughts only           -> Thinking { reasoning: None }
  {$patch:{toolCalls:[{id}]}}              -> TrackedToolFinished{ id }
  {$set:...} / {$rewindTo:...} / info|error|warning -> ignored
  Completed -> never emitted (Gemini has no turn-end record); the session deactivates through the existing 4s TerminalCandidate debounce.

TOOL LABEL TABLE (Gemini-specific; the shared classify_tool() would mislabel 'replace' as "Using development tools")
  read_file, read_many_files, list_directory -> "Reading project files"
  write_file, replace                        -> "Editing files"
  run_shell_command                          -> classify_tool(name, args.command) so cargo build/test/clippy/fmt, npm test/build, git status, rg, python special-cases still apply ("Running command" default)
  glob, grep_search                          -> "Searching project"
  google_web_search, web_fetch               -> "Browsing documentation"
  write_todos, enter_plan_mode, exit_plan_mode -> "Planning changes"
  ask_user                                   -> "Waiting for input"
  activate_skill, invoke_agent               -> "Running coding agent"
  everything else                            -> "Using development tools"
  file basename: reuse events::extract_file_basename(args) (already reads 'file_path' and 'path'); language: language_from_file(). Never read args.content / old_string / new_string / raw command.

WATCHER.RS / MAIN.RS CHANGES
  watcher.rs: NONE required. The format is append-only newline-delimited JSON, so LogTailer works verbatim. recent_logs() depth is fine: tmp(0)/slug(1)/chats(2)/file(3) and tmp(0)/slug(1)/chats(2)/parentId(3)/file(4) are both within the max depth of 5, and the skip-list ('node_modules','target','scratch','steps','tasks') conveniently excludes the Gemini 'tasks' tracker dir. The only required change is the path-aware is_session_log in provider.rs (see above) plus the two main.rs call-site changes for the path-aware project resolution.
  main.rs: (1) switch the two parse_line_for call sites to parse_line_for_path so the Gemini adapter can resolve the project from the path; (2) nothing else — no new watcher, no new dependency.
  No SQLite crate, no zstd changes, no new Cargo dependency.

FORMAT-CHURN RISK AND FAIL-SAFE
  Churn points observed: (a) .json single-document -> .jsonl append-only; (b) project dir sha256 hash -> human slug (ProjectRegistry migration moves the old hash dir to the new slug dir); (c) filename 'session-<ts>-<shortId>.jsonl' plus collision index; (d) legacy .json files are migrated in place on resume.
  Fail-safe design:
   - Anchor the matcher on the DIRECTORY SHAPE ('chats'), not on the filename, so (a) and (c) do not break it.
   - Accept only .jsonl, so the line-delimited tailer can never mis-parse a legacy .json document; if a .json file appears, ignore it rather than guess.
   - Treat an unrecognised record shape as a no-op (return an empty Vec) instead of erroring, so a future field rename degrades to "no activity" rather than to garbage presence.
   - Never emit a label, file or model that is not on an explicit allow-list; unknown tool names collapse to "Using development tools".
   - Never read prompt/response/thought/result/summary fields; the allow-list makes a future upstream change fail closed (missing field -> no event) rather than open.
   - If the .project_root marker is missing, fall back to the slug (still only a folder name) instead of guessing or publishing a path.
   - If the metadata record cannot be parsed, skip the file rather than emitting a session with an unknown project.
  Residual risk: upstream could rename the 'chats' directory or move sessions to a different store; detect it by watching for new .jsonl files under ~/.gemini/tmp and failing open to the focused-app presence rather than to a wrong project.

summary: Gemini CLI DOES write a local, machine-readable, append-only activity log and is viable at the full "rich" level. Sessions are stored as newline-delimited JSON under %USERPROFILE%\.gemini\tmp\<project-slug>\chats\session-<YYYY-MM-DDTHH-mm>-<shortSessionId>.jsonl (subagents in chats\<parentSessionId>\<subagentSessionId>.jsonl), appended live with fs.appendFileSync on every turn and tool batch. Each line is a self-describing JSON record: the first is session metadata (sessionId, projectHash, startTime, lastUpdated, kind), later lines are message records {id, timestamp (RFC3339), type: user|gemini, content, model, toolCalls[{id,name,args,result,status,timestamp}]} plus {$set}/{$patch}/{$rewindTo} patch records. That yields project, model id, current file basename (args.file_path), normalized tool activity (toolCalls[].name), phase and an elapsed timer, all without ever shipping prompts, responses, thoughts, tool args bodies, tool results, shell commands or full paths. Two caveats: (1) the main-session record does NOT contain the workspace path — it must be recovered from the sibling marker file <root>/<slug>/.project_root or %USERPROFILE%\.gemini\projects.json (the in-file projectHash is a one-way sha256); (2) tool calls are only persisted when they COMPLETE, so the presence lags a running tool by its duration. The existing LogTailer needs no changes; only provider.rs (new variant, path-aware is_session_log) and a small path-aware project resolution in main.rs are required. No new Rust dependency.
